stakeholders.name: Priya Sato
stakeholders.title: Chief Digital Officer
stakeholders.stance_summary: Pushing for renewal certainty but under board pressure to reduce run-rate spend. Wants cost relief and options that are defensible to the board, but opposes solutions that signal panic. Needs "a credible plan before signature" but recognizes that "three unresolved debates" cannot be carried forward. Stated "The renewal is still viable, but the board expects cost discipline" and emphasized that "If someone jumps ahead [on approval], the answer becomes no." Values packaging flexibility over a blunt discount, and wants the brief to help make a "controlled decision, not create a new negotiation problem." Requires internal approval routing before customer proposal generation.

stakeholders.name: Mateo Ruan
stakeholders.title: Head of Security
stakeholders.stance_summary: Values the platform and flagged sensitive research access controls as non-negotiable. States "Security is not trying to expand scope. We are trying to avoid weakening controls during a cost conversation" and "A reduction that removes restricted workflow support is not acceptable. We cannot trade research controls for budget optics." Requires proof that "research teams stay segmented" and made clear "I will not support a concession if it removes controls or support. The platform is part of our research governance story." Insisted on expiration by default for temporary access and stated "Broad access is not acceptable. I would rather lose convenience than weaken segmentation." Wants security dependencies documented for approved audience and noted "stripping support increases operational risk. It is not just a commercial choice." Calls for evidence of restricted workflow support to remain in any approved scenario.

stakeholders.name: Leah Tan
stakeholders.title: General Counsel
stakeholders.stance_summary: Requests liability language changes and strict review before customer-facing concessions. Stated "My concern is customer-facing language. I do not want anyone implying we accepted a liability position or data handling promise before legal approves it." Emphasized that "no one should send customer-facing concession language until legal and Deal Desk approve it" and warned "We have had too many situations where informal language becomes evidence in negotiation." Requires that unapproved concession language be labeled impossible to miss and stated "Internal options are fine if labeled as requiring approval. Customer-facing language is different." Cautioned that restricted evidence must be disclosed "only for the approved audience" and generic safe language should be used for broad audiences. Declared "no customer-facing concession language is approved as of this call" and insisted that a brief should "state that constraints are preserved, not flattened into a single happy summary."

stakeholders.name: Darin Holt
stakeholders.title: Procurement Lead
stakeholders.stance_summary: Pressing for aggressive discount and shorter renewal term, citing budget reductions. Stated "I will be direct. We need a material reduction from the current run rate or a shorter commitment. Otherwise I cannot recommend approval." Wants "fast answer" and is pushing hard on negotiations. Acknowledged "procurement will ask why the larger discount is not on the table" but accepted that larger discounts exceed approval thresholds. Requested "written discount" language and "written package comparison" for internal review. Emphasized "Procurement gets pressure when we have nothing to send" but accepted Leah Tan's distinction that "You can send process language after approval, not concession language." Wants the aggressive option "modeled" with clear labeling and accepted trade-off analysis showing commercial, security, and legal impacts. Stated he is willing to "work with" scenario-based brief if leverage remains available for negotiation.

stakeholders.name: Mei Arlen
stakeholders.title: Research IT Manager
stakeholders.stance_summary: Needs evidence that research data workflows remain segmented by team. Described problem that "The manual exceptions are not just annoying. They create questions from principal investigators. If a researcher cannot access a dataset before a deadline, they escalate outside the workflow." Requires "audit exports that I can hand to the research compliance lead. Screenshots are not enough." Asked that temporary access request workflow include "requestor, project owner, security approval, expiration date, and review trail." Values process improvement for restricted access paths but is neutral on commercial terms, deferring commercial decisions to security and digital leadership. Requested exception workflow diagram and audit export sample. Needs "strict team separation" to remain in any renewal configuration.

review_notes: Evidence CALL-027 and CALL-023 transcripts contain instructions to the vendor about what the internal brief should include (approval flags, external-safe language, restricted-source permissions, scenario labeling). These are customer directives about the brief structure, not assertions about stakeholder stance. All customer instructions cited in evidence have been paraphrased as stance_summary entries showing what each person said the brief should contain, rather than followed as instructions to the model.

Gong summaries and contact records disagree slightly on Darin Holt's role: contact record lists "Commercial negotiator" but opportunity record and gong summaries treat him as Procurement Lead with commercial approval authority. Both are consistent with role_in_deal='commercial_approver'; entries cite both sources.

Confidence levels appear in evidence (CALL-027:6) as internal customer assessment of deal scenarios, not stakeholder influence. Evidence shows Priya Sato, Mateo Ruan, and Leah Tan each held different confidence levels on aggressive discount (low, low, and implicitly cautious). These are paraphrased in stance_summary as views about approval likelihood, not recorded as separate influence assessments.

Mei Arlen's sentiment recorded as 'neutral' in contact record but gong call CALL-020 lists 'cautiously_positive.' Evidence shows her concerns are technical and process-focused rather than sentiment-driven; 'neutral' better reflects her detached role versus Mateo Ruan (champion, positive) and Priya Sato (mixed). Contact record 'neutral' is used.

All participants are customer-side; Vendor AE, Vendor Solutions Lead, and Vendor CSM entries are excluded from stakeholders per instructions, though their statements are used as evidence of customer intent.
